text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- In a critical National Security Council meeting the head of the Turkish armed forces and four force commanders will tell the Islamist-led government's leaders of their concern over the rise of religous movements in Turkey.
- The head of the Turkish armed forces backs President Suleyman Demirel's statements highlightining the risks against the current secular and democratic regime.
- The far-rightist leader of the Nationalist Action Party warns university students in his organisation not to go to school for a week amid rising tension at universities.
- Four ministers from the Islamist wing of the coalition say they are prepared to resign in order to dispel the tension they caused after making radical Islamist statements.
- Turkey declared Iran's consul to Erzurum "persona non grata" after he criticised anti-Iranian statements made by a senior army commander during a visit to the United States.
- Turks are planing to hold referendum to decide whether to carry on a month-old blackout campaign to pressurise the government to bring a security scandal into light.
- Markets are calm despite the prolonged tension in politics.

- Leftist university students are planning to demonstrate near a mosque in central Istanbul while Islamists and right-wingers attend Friday prayers following a week of tension and sporadic clashes between the groups at Istanbul University.
